title: Training Controllable World Models via Action Influence Maximization
abstract: arXiv:2610.27387v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Action-conditioned video generative models trained on successful, goal-directed demonstrations tend to ignore the commanded action, rendering a plausible expert-like future regardless of what is asked of them. We trace this failure to training data that lack sufficient action influence. We analyze this metric and prove that it upper bounds the action influence that any model trained on that data can express. Expert demonstrations, whose narrow action distributions let next states be predicted without attending to the action, set a low ceiling that no amount of model capacity alone can raise. Raising it requires collecting different data. We introduce Action Influence Maximization (AIM), an algorithm for actively collecting training data for improving dataset action influence. We compare the performance and data-efficiency of AIM against exploration heuristics and intrinsic-motivation methods on simulated navigation and manipulation tas

translated_title: 通过动作影响力最大化训练可控世界模型
translated_abstract: 在成功的目标导向演示数据上训练的动作条件视频生成模型往往会忽略所指令的动作，无论要求它们做什么，都会生成一个看似合理、类似专家的未来预测。我们将这一失败归因于训练数据缺乏足够的动作影响力。我们分析了这一度量指标，并证明它上界了在该数据上训练的任何模型所能表达的动作影响力。专家演示的狭窄动作分布使得无需关注动作即可预测下一状态，从而设定了一个较低的上限，仅靠增加模型容量无法突破。要提高这一上限，需要收集不同的数据。我们提出了动作影响力最大化，这是一种用于主动收集训练数据以提升数据集动作影响力的算法。我们在模拟导航和操作任务上将AIM的性能和数据效率与探索启发式方法及内在动机方法进行了比较。
tldr: 论文提出动作影响力最大化算法，通过主动收集具有高动作影响力的训练数据，突破专家演示数据的动作影响力上限，从而解决世界模型忽略指令动作的问题，实现更可控的动作条件视频生成世界模型。
